es-sustained-listen-llamada.role: Phase 6.1A sustained listening passage — a two-voice phone call rendered entirely by on-device speech synthesis at lesson time (no audio file is shipped)
es-sustained-listen-llamada.declaredUrl: n/a — no recording; the passage lives as five section texts in Condisco/Content/packs/spanish.json under sustainedListenings[0]
es-sustained-listen-llamada.transcript: The full five-section text (Elena ↔ Diego) as authored in the pack's transcript field; section texts are the same words the synthesizer speaks.
es-sustained-listen-llamada.note: Declared voice ids are preferences, not requirements: when a declared identifier is not installed on the learner's device, the section is spoken by any installed voice whose language matches the section's languageCode (documented on SustainedListeningSection.voiceId in Condisco/Models/CoursePack.swift). A missing voice can never make a section unspeakable. Voice availability varies by device and iOS version, so no static audio hash exists.

sequence: es-sustained-listen-llamada — presented by the new step es-a2-imperfecto-step-listen (purpose notice, sustainedListeningId es-sustained-listen-llamada, launch activity es-sustained-listen-llamada-launch) inserted between es-a2-imperfecto-step-rb8 and the final-response step rb9, which stays the lesson terminal. The view lane (6.1B) hides the transcript on the first pass, offers per-section replay at normal/slow speed, reveals the transcript on demand, and grades the three embedded questions (main idea / key detail / speaker intent) with fixed-answer selection logic.
delivery: device-speech — intentionally NOT shipped as a recording. AudioStimulus-style on-device AVSpeechSynthesizer rendering from the authored section texts; the passage is a data-level construct (sections + voice ids + transcript), so no entry is needed in tools/device-speech-media.txt (that allowlist covers MediaItem assets; this passage declares no media items).
